newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - July 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - July 9.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Hashoo group has agreed to deposit an amount of 1.2 billion rupees with the government against its outstanding loans.
- The government has denied reports Pakistan had cancelled a deal of purchasing tanks from Ukraine.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has asked the coalition partners in the Sindh government to increase cooperation so that the law and order situation in Karachi could be improved.

- The five-member IMF delegation due in Islamabad on Wednesday for a two week visit will review new structural reforms measures taken in the budget and discuss the extension of general sales tax to the retail level.
- Four countries, including Pakistan, have asked Thailand for possible assistance in evacuating their nationals from strife-torn Cambodia, diplomats said.
- The U.S. State Department said Washington wanted the release of its DEA employee in Pakistan, Ayaz Baloch.
- Nawaz Sharif said a huge amount of money is being pumped into the country to create chaotic conditions and destabilise the political system and the economy.
- The Muslim Commercial Bank has lowered its mark-up rate by 1.09 percent effective from July 1.
- The State (central) Bank has asked all banks and development finance institutions to prepare cases against the defaulters not contacting them to settle their dues.
- After a gap of almost five months, two new stocks are coming up at the Karachi Stock Exchange.
